description:
The lightest and most versatile long-tail Cargo Bike in the world. Having the lowest center of gravity means easiest to ride with a load. The frame adjusts to fit people 4ft 6in to 6ft 4in. One bike the whole family can ride, and it’s hand made in Oregon, U.S.A..

The Bike Friday Haul-A-Day cargo bike is incredibly capable and versatile. Customers all over the world continue to amaze and inspire us with stories and pictures of how they use their Haul-a-Day cargo bikes daily, fully loaded with two kids, gear, beer, tents, well everything, and even the kitchen sink sometimes.

The base model Haul-a-Day, without e-assist, comes with a double chainring to get you a good gear range for any outing (18 speeds). Even with this wide gear range, the Haul-a-Day is the lightest cargo bike on the market starting at 35lbs. For 2022 we have doubled the front end stiffness for increased confidence and control with a heavy load.

If you add Electric Assist, you’ll be ready for any load, hill, or distance! with the 1 by 9 speed drivetrain and the powerful mid-drive motor.

The only long-tail cargo bike built in the U.S.A.

The lightest long-tail cargo bike built today. For perspective…other top brands weigh 10-25lbs more for the same carrying capacity. You can actually lift this bike!

The frame adjusts to a wide range of sizes to fit your whole family. It truly adjusts to your future needs.

Fits on many transport racks: bus, car, and train. It even stands upright on its rear end for easy storage

The frame can be disassembled for packing/travel

Standard bike built to carry up to 420 pounds (190kg), Heavy Load upgrade is available to 510 pounds (231kg)(Load = rider and cargo)

Compatible with a wide range of accessories, from Bike Friday and other brands like Yepp.

components.description: For children under 6: compatible with up to two Thule Yepp Maxi seats, adapter required For children over 4: Whoopee-Deux Bar, Whoopee Cushion, Big Foot Rests w/ Cargo Rails
Fits on many transport racks: bus, car, and train (tested with Yakima and Thule roof-rack and tested on a local bus (LTD) front-load bike-rack)
